expansion:
Option A is correct. This presentation represents diabetic macular oedema with cystoid macular oedema affecting the centre of the macula. The lecture describes diffuse diabetic maculopathy as having “Frequent cystoid macular oedema” and lists “intra vitreal injection” (L19.1, page 13). Its treatment page explicitly includes “Intra vitreal Injection of anti VEGEF” (L19.1, page 15). Thus intravitreal anti-VEGF injections are the keyed pharmacologic treatment; they reduce VEGF-driven retinal vascular leakage and macular oedema (not taken from the course material). There is a course discrepancy: the cited treatment bullet is printed under grid treatment for diffuse retinal thickening “more than 500 µ-m from centre of fovea,” whereas this vignette specifies centre involvement; the printed key remains A.

Option B is wrong. Topical beta-blockers lower intraocular pressure by reducing aqueous-humour production and are used in glaucoma; they do not treat retinal vascular leakage or diabetic macular oedema (not taken from the course material).

Option C is wrong. Systemic corticosteroids are not the current standard first-line pharmacologic treatment for diabetic centre-involving macular oedema. Although steroids can be used in selected retinal inflammatory conditions or as local ocular therapy in some macular-oedema settings, they carry important systemic adverse effects in a diabetic patient and do not replace intravitreal anti-VEGF treatment here (not taken from the course material).

Option D is wrong. Pilocarpine is a cholinergic miotic that can increase trabecular aqueous outflow in selected glaucoma situations; it has no role in treating diabetic cystoid macular oedema (not taken from the course material).
objective: Identify intravitreal anti-VEGF injection as the pharmacologic treatment for diabetic macular oedema with cystoid centre involvement.
